sources.title: Mobile Matters 2024 — Chart data
facts: Ofcom lists separate chart data for the 2024 report.
The file supports checking published aggregate values.
Historical chart data is not current parcel-level service evidence.

sources.title: Mobile Matters Interactive report 2024
facts: Ofcom retains an interactive report for the 2024 Mobile Matters release.
The interactive is a presentation of prior-vintage mobile-experience analysis.
It should be used for trend and context only with vintage separation.

sources.title: Mobile coverage obligations
facts: Ofcom's page records Shared Rural Network coverage obligations and nation-specific thresholds.
It distinguishes obligations due in 2024 from further thresholds due by 31 January 2027.
Obligation thresholds and licence conditions are regulatory requirements, not proof of current orderability at every address.

sources.title: Shared Rural Network Coverage Obligations — assessment of geographic coverage compliance
sources.lines: official assessment link at HTML lines 159-166
facts: Ofcom published a 2024 assessment of operators' compliance with geographic SRN coverage obligations.
The assessment concerns regulatory thresholds measured under an Ofcom methodology.
Compliance at aggregate geographic thresholds does not establish service at a particular premises.

sources.title: Shared Rural Network Coverage Obligations — 2024 assessment update for Three
facts: Ofcom published a separate update after further assessment of information supplied by Three.
The page states that Ofcom confirmed the relevant requirements had been met after the original assessment timing.
The update is operator-compliance evidence and must remain separate from local real-world performance.

sources.title: Shared Rural Network compliance methodology
facts: Ofcom identifies the methodology used to measure compliance with SRN coverage obligations.
The methodology was updated in July 2025 after earlier versions in 2020, 2021 and 2024.
Methodology evidence governs regulatory compliance interpretation and is not itself a coverage result.

sources.title: Letter to BT EE — assessment of initial radio plan for 2020 coverage obligations
sources.lines: official letter listing at HTML lines 174-180
facts: Ofcom lists a separate assessment letter for EE's initial SRN radio plan.
The letter relates to a plan submitted to show how future coverage commitments would be met.
An initial radio plan is planning and compliance evidence, not current service evidence.

sources.title: Letter to Hutchison 3G UK — assessment of initial radio plan for 2020 coverage obligations
sources.lines: official letter listing at HTML lines 174-180
facts: Ofcom lists a separate assessment letter for Three's initial SRN radio plan.
The document records regulatory review of a forward delivery plan.
Plan assessment must not be represented as completed local coverage.

sources.title: Letter to Telefónica UK — assessment of initial radio plan for 2020 coverage obligations
sources.lines: official letter listing at HTML lines 174-180
facts: Ofcom lists a separate assessment letter for O2's initial SRN radio plan.
The letter belongs to the initial-plan compliance record.
Forward radio-plan evidence cannot establish current parcel availability.

sources.title: Letter to Vodafone — assessment of initial radio plan for 2020 coverage obligations
sources.lines: official letter listing at HTML lines 174-180
facts: Ofcom lists a separate assessment letter for Vodafone's initial SRN radio plan.
The document assesses a plan for meeting coverage obligations.
Regulatory planning evidence is distinct from measured current service.

sources.title: Individual mobile licences containing SRN coverage obligations
facts: Ofcom links the individual spectrum licences that give legal effect to operator coverage commitments.
The licence framework contains operator and nation-specific obligations.
Licence conditions establish duties and thresholds, not exact address-level service status.

sources.title: Quality and methodology information: Shared Rural Network — publication page
facts: BDUK published the SRN quality and methodology information on 24 December 2025.
The publication is intended to support interpretation of SRN data releases.
It describes strengths, limitations and methods so users can avoid misuse.

sources.title: Quality and methodology information: Shared Rural Network
facts: The QMI states that SRN reporting presents premises, roads and other locations forecast to receive 4G uplift from subsidised delivery.
The document distinguishes forecast uplift reporting from observed current service.
Quality characteristics and methodological limitations must be retained when using the release.

sources.title: Shared Rural Network Wellbeing Survey — publication page
facts: BDUK published the Shared Rural Network Wellbeing Survey on 15 January 2026.
The publication describes a baseline survey of 1,285 residents of households and businesses expected to benefit from SRN delivery.
The survey is evaluation evidence and not a mobile-coverage measurement dataset.

sources.title: Shared Rural Network Wellbeing Survey Wave 1 Findings report
facts: The report presents baseline findings and states that a follow-up survey is intended to measure change.
The sample covers locations where enhanced mobile broadband connectivity is being provided by the SRN programme.
Baseline self-reported usage and wellbeing findings must not be treated as exact network coverage.

sources.title: Mobile Supplier Additionality Research
facts: The research examines benefits associated with moving from no operator to one operator and from one to multiple operators in rural communities.
The report highlights limited localised actual usage data and says a mast near a community does not necessarily mean every premises benefits.
It is research on additionality and awareness, not an SRN impact evaluation or exact coverage dataset.
